# ARM v2: architecture tolls meet a production-silicon transition

Research cutoff: **2026-10-19 UTC**. This is an isolated research/onboarding package, not a live Site change or investment recommendation. All monetary financials are USD millions unless stated. Fiscal years end March 31; FY2027 Q1 ended June 30, 2026. Eligible US Nasdaq security: **ARM ADS**, one ADS representing **one ordinary share**, supported by [annual cover](https://investors.arm.com/node/8281/html) and the [official Robinhood stock page](https://robinhood.com/us/en/stocks/ARM/). Tradability is not a suitability judgment.

## Bottom line and valuation boundary

Arm's established business monetizes processor architecture and design through upfront/license-related revenue and subsequent per-chip royalties. The important new uncertainty is its move into physical production silicon through the AGI CPU. That creates a second economic model with manufacturing commitments, inventory and customer conflicts. The existing high gross-margin licensing model cannot simply be applied to silicon revenue.

The model produces conditional dated-anchor values of **$8.48 bear / $25.46 base / $62.42 bull per ADS**, with approximately **74% / 78% / 83%** of enterprise value coming from terminal value. These are scenario outputs, not price targets, probabilities or forecasts of trading prices. No current stock price has been verified, and no upside/downside or present market-cap comparison is asserted. The capital anchor is March 31, 2026, with exact shares and audited balance sheet; the information set extends to October 19. This is deliberately a restated-date conditional appraisal, **not a historical backtest and not an October19 valuation**. The later DreamBig acquisition is reserved in the bridge. A live publication with a current target requires a fully refreshed capital/share bridge and stub cash flows.

The economic model expenses SBC and R&D. It does not turn non-GAAP earnings into free owner cash by adding back employee equity costs. Cost and reinvestment assumptions, rather than an optimistic TAM multiple, explain the wide range. Every valid path is replayable from dcf-inputs-v2.json and replay_dcf.py within this v2 folder.

## Business quality, mix and competitive position

FY2026 revenue was $4,920: $2,613 royalty (53.1%) and $2,307 license/other (46.9%). FY2025 had $2,168 and $1,839 respectively; FY2024 $1,802 and $1,431. Licensing is not uniformly recurring: delivery, renewal, high-value customer agreements, service performance and backlog timing matter. Royalty revenue depends on customers' chip shipments, mix, contractual rates and reporting. Higher Armv9 and compute-subsystem adoption can increase monetization per chip without commensurate end-market shipment growth. These mechanisms differ from claiming all AI chip spending becomes Arm revenue. [FY2026 20-F, revenue recognition, segment and revenue-disaggregation notes](https://investors.arm.com/node/8281/html)

The architecture/software ecosystem creates switching and porting costs, broad tool support and partner familiarity. That does not eliminate competing architectures, RISC-V, x86, custom designs or customer bargaining power. Architectural licenses and product licenses have differing economics and timing. Long design cycles can lengthen royalty persistence but delay the payoff from R&D. A useful forecast needs separately tested chip-volume, per-chip royalty uplift, product-mix and licensing assumptions; undisclosed contract rates prevent a precise unit-level bottom-up model here.

June-quarter FY2027 revenue was $1,289, comprising $715 royalty and $574 license/other. ACV was $1,732, up13%, versus revenue growth22%; annualized contract value and recognized license revenue should not be conflated. Management says data-center royalties more than doubled; the filing does not provide a complete audited end-market profit split. The quarter's $91 GAAP EBIT (7.1% margin) versus $531 non-GAAP EBIT (41.2%) underscores how employee equity and exclusions affect apparent economics. [July29 results](https://investors.arm.com/node/8356/html)

## The silicon change: observe capacity, cash and customer conflicts

Arm announced AGI CPU production silicon in March2026; the annual filing says it had no material FY2026 revenue effect. Management's July29 letter says initial product had been delivered to multiple customers, capacity secured for its original $1bn FY2027–28 opportunity, and demand now exceeded $2bn. **Demand/pipeline is not booked revenue, audited backlog, a take-or-pay customer commitment or secured manufacturing capacity for $2bn.** The model does not treat $2bn as guaranteed sales. [Annual risk factors](https://investors.arm.com/node/8281/html), [July29 letter](https://investors.arm.com/node/8356/html)

In the July29 call, management described $193m of quarterly technology/licensing/design-services contribution from the SoftBank agreement and an approximately $200m quarterly run-rate expectation for the remainder of the year. These are management statements, not independent demand evidence. The same call frames supply capacity and customer mix as constraints. [Company-hosted July29 transcript, pages4–5](https://investors.arm.com/static-files/2ef5e3bf-f276-4a46-a4a2-2aadccd6710b). Only concise research interpretation is retained; the licensed transcript is linked rather than reproduced.

Production silicon can let Arm capture more value per deployment, but it may compete with customers who historically paid to use its IP. It introduces qualification, wafer/packaging/test, supply concentration, yield, warranty, inventory obsolescence, cash-conversion and order-cancellation risks. The annual filing describes approximately $100m of near-term semiconductor supply purchase commitments under an agreement and warns these could grow materially. Non-cancelable cloud/data-center/software/services obligations totaled approximately $1,056.5m through2036. These are operating commitments, not automatically debt to subtract in addition to operating costs and investment. [20-F risk factors and commitments note](https://investors.arm.com/node/8281/html)

September8's Neoverse CSS N4/AGI update describes ecosystem activity and Volcano Engine's agentic sandbox deployment. Treat this as technical/commercial validation, not additional quantified contracted revenue. [Arm September8 update](https://newsroom.arm.com/news/arm-agi-cpu-neoverse-css-n4-agentic-ai)

The bear/base/bull model assumes FY2027–28 silicon revenue totaling $350m/$1,000m/$1,800m, respectively, with different ramp and margin trajectories. The base aligns with the originally discussed opportunity rather than all stated demand; the bull requires incremental supply and execution. Silicon EBIT margins begin negative and mature to10%/20%/27%; no pure-IP gross margin is assigned to chips. All three trajectories are analyst assumptions. No separate licensing royalty is counted on Arm's own silicon shipments in the model.

## Management: evidence of execution and limits of inference

Rene Haas and Jason Child sign the latest results. Nine consecutive quarters from Q1 FY2025 through Q1 FY2027 are compared with the issuer's preceding revenue/EPS ranges and approximate opex guidance in guidance-vs-actual-v2.csv. Four revenues and five non-GAAP EPS results exceeded their stated ranges; none fell below. This supports an assessment of cautious near-term guidance and consistent execution, not a quantified decade-long management premium. Approximate opex estimates are recorded without pretending they are hard ranges. Company-reproduced guidance is cross-checked against adjacent releases where available. [Q1 FY2025](https://investors.arm.com/node/7256/html), [Q2 FY2025](https://investors.arm.com/node/7406/html), [Q3 FY2025](https://investors.arm.com/node/7481/html), [Q1 FY2026](https://investors.arm.com/node/7626/html), [Q2 FY2026](https://investors.arm.com/node/7711/html), [Q3 FY2026](https://investors.arm.com/node/7826/html), [Q4 FY2026](https://investors.arm.com/node/8141/html), [Q1 FY2027](https://investors.arm.com/node/8356/html)

FY2025 revenue guidance initially $3.8–4.1bn narrowed to $3.94–4.04bn by Q3; annual actual was $4.007bn. Non-GAAP EPS $1.63 was within the final $1.56–1.64 range. Short-term guidance accuracy should not substitute for independently verifying AGI unit economics, related-party collections or whether compensation-adjusted returns on new investment exceed capital cost.

Annual FY2026 revenue rose22.8%, but GAAP EBIT rose8.3%, and GAAP operating margin fell20.7%→18.3%. R&D rose$2,071m→$2,776m, or approximately34%. Total cash flow improved materially, but contract assets and related-party exposure also rose. This combination supports investment-led growth while rejecting a simplistic immediate operating-leverage story. Executive financial performance measures use non-GAAP metrics; incentives can favor growth/exclusions that ordinary-share owners must evaluate economically. [20-F operating review and remuneration discussion](https://investors.arm.com/node/8281/html)

## China, SoftBank and governance

Arm China is not controlled by Arm or SoftBank, and Arm relies on its separate counterparty for licensing into China, royalty reporting, collection and contractual compliance. Arm's10% nonvoting Acetone interest, with Acetone holding48.2% of Arm China, is an approximately4.8% indirect economic stake. It is not a consolidated48.2% ownership position. Arm China revenue was $790.6m in FY2026 (16.1% of total), $670.4m FY2025 and $670.8m FY2024; its concentration is not identical to all PRC geographic revenue. FY2026 service-share costs were$63.3m; net amount due was$276.2m, and the associated credit-loss allowance was$28.3m. The filing discloses past information/access and collection issues. [20-F Note20 and China risk factors](https://investors.arm.com/node/8281/html)

Total related-party revenue was$1,499m,30.5% of FY2026 sales, versus$823m FY2025. External-customer sales grew only7%, while related-party sales grew82%. The SoftBank-affiliate technology/service arrangement contributed$704.4m revenue in FY2026 and$645.8m current contract assets. Contract assets reflect earned but not yet billable revenue; they are not cash. A robust bull case must demonstrate ultimate cash collection and external demand, not merely larger intragroup commitments. These figures must not be added to Arm China revenue again when describing total related-party exposure. [20-F operating review/Note20](https://investors.arm.com/node/8281/html)

SoftBank beneficially owned922,733,999 shares, approximately86.4%, on May21,2026, when ordinary shares totaled1,068,078,760. SoftBank's September23 offering memorandum reports86.4% at June30. The approximately14% non-SoftBank balance is **not verified freely trading float**: other affiliate, plan, restricted and ownership considerations remain. Low effective float can affect trading volatility without changing enterprise cash flows. SoftBank control creates conflicts over related-party deals, board influence, acquisitions and monetization. Its pledged-share financing is SoftBank borrowing, not Arm corporate debt. The memorandum describes September expansion to$25bn of the Arm-share-backed margin facility; do not load that debt onto Arm's bridge. [20-F ownership](https://investors.arm.com/node/8281/html), [SoftBank September23 offering memorandum](https://links.sgx.com/FileOpen/SoftBank%20Group%20Corp.%20-%20Offering%20Memorandum%20dated%2023%20September%202026.ashx?App=Prospectus&FileID=71217)

## Litigation and acquisitions: dated, limited claims

Arm's October13 statement says a jury found for it on four Qualcomm claims and awarded Qualcomm $1 on each of its other two claims. That is Arm's account of the specified verdict, not a finding that all Qualcomm/Arm disputes or future appeals and business consequences are resolved. No litigation-win revenue uplift is embedded. [Arm October13 statement](https://newsroom.arm.com/news/arm-qualcomm-legal-dispute)

The full June30 6-K reports DreamBig closed July1,2026 for approximately$265m. The March31 model reserves the nominal $265m later cash purchase at time zero. This conservative analyst reserve convention does not discount the July1 outflow and is not exact transaction present value; acquired cash/liabilities and final adjustments are not separately modeled. It does not treat the acquisition as pending or subtract it again in forecast investment. Expected product synergy is not separately valued. [Q1 full financial statements, subsequent-events note](https://investors.arm.com/node/8361/html)

The package includes ten fiscal slots FY2017–26, **six comparable/reconstructed US-GAAP annual periods FY2021–26**, and a separate four-year historical SoftBank segment revenue series. The latter totals$1,689m/$1,831m/$1,836m/$1,898m for years ended March2017/18/19/20. FY2017 is pro forma spanning pre-acquisition periods. Earlier software/services scope, Arm China deconsolidation, acquisitions and accounting differ; these are **not spliced into a ten-year comparable CAGR**. Private ownership does not mean no public information, but a complete comparable older cash/return history is unavailable in this package. [SoftBank FY2018 report](https://group.softbank/system/files/pdf/ir/financials/financial_reports/financial-report_q4fy2017_01_en.pdf), [SoftBank FY2020 report](https://group.softbank/system/files/pdf/ir/financials/financial_reports/financial-report_q4fy2019_01_en.pdf), [IPO financials](https://investors.arm.com/node/6546/html)

Continuing revenue/EBIT are separated from consolidated net income: FY2021 continuing net income$544m versus consolidated$388m includes$156m discontinued loss; FY2022$676m versus$549m includes$127m discontinued loss. Historical CFO/DA/SBC may include discontinued activities. FY2021 CFO also benefited from a one-time $750m non-cancellable, non-refundable customer prepayment disclosed in the IPO cash-flow discussion; it is not a normal annual cash run-rate. IPO-year accelerated award recognition and changing cash-versus-equity compensation prevent naive SBC trend extrapolation.

FY2026 CFO$1,524m minus PPE cash purchases$545m is$979m, **not Arm's reported FCF**. After$30m intangible purchases and$67m intangible-obligation payments, reported FCF is$882m. FY2025 corresponding FCF was$99m. These definitions explain why treating capital-light as zero capital expenditure fails. FY2026 CFO also adds back$1,052m equity compensation and is sensitive to tax and collection timing; withholding taxes on vested awards consumed another$529m in financing. Q1 FY2027 CFO$902m yielded reported FCF$665m after$197m PPE,$11m intangibles and$29m obligations, with$278m withholding financing outflow. These quarterly collection benefits are not annualized. [Annual cash flow](https://investors.arm.com/node/8281/html), [Q1 full 6-K](https://investors.arm.com/node/8361/html)

## Capital bridge and compensation convention

March31 capital bridge: cash/short investments$3,601m minus finance leases$59m, existing EDA liabilities$175m ($78m current+$97m noncurrent), DreamBig reserve$265m and minimum operating cash$246m = **$2,856m** net nonoperating value. All $387m of equity investments are assigned zero bridge value, including $96m of publicly listed holdings and $291m of other holdings. This is a conservative exclusion of both quoted and unquoted investments, not a claim that all excluded holdings are illiquid or included in cash. Including quoted holdings requires consistent valuation, tax and claim adjustments. Operating lease liabilities$432m are not deducted because rent remains in modeled operating costs; switching to lease-capitalized accounting requires a consistent EBIT/reinvestment adjustment.

The denominator is exactly1,064,055,252 March31 ordinary shares, equivalent to1,064.055252m ADS. It is neither the EPS diluted weighted average1,068m nor a market-cap-derived proxy. June30 ordinary shares1,068m are rounded and June-quarter diluted weighted average1,078m is not a point-in-time count. Both are later disclosures, not silent replacements for the exact March anchor.

March31 disclosed awards outstanding/expected to vest are approximately1m2022-plan RSUs plus18m Omnibus awards. June30 Omnibus awards rise to24m; disclosures exclude PSUs without established grant dates. June unrecognized Omnibus compensation is$3,621.9m over1.6years versus March$1,719.3m over1.2years. The425,000 VCP PSUs are already inside Omnibus, not an additional layer to add blindly. Plan headroom is not outstanding dilution. [Annual Note13](https://investors.arm.com/node/8281/html), [June6-K award note](https://investors.arm.com/node/8361/html)

Baseline valuation retains cash-equivalent economic SBC in margins, with fixed March shares. It represents a replacement-compensation convention, not precise legal allocation between existing shares and awards. Separate±5pp/−10pp economic margin sensitivities and a19m extra-denominator diagnostic expose compensation risk. The latter may overlap expenses already charged and omits ungranted PSUs: it is not a complete maximum dilution bound. A grant-by-grant fair-value/vesting model is still needed for a precise award claim. No claim of zero actual future dilution is made.

## DCF assumptions, consistency and funding

Three revenue streams are projected for FY2027–36. Royalty growth begins14%/24%/32%; license growth2%/10%/15%; both fade annually to terminal2.5%/3%/3.5%. Silicon sales are explicit arrays rather than an invented starting growth rate from zero. Final-year silicon growth also converges to terminal growth. Mature IP EBIT margins22%/34%/42% and silicon10%/20%/27% are conditional economic margins inclusive of employee compensation and expensed R&D. At23% normalized tax, no recurring tax windfall is assumed and loss years generate no immediate tax refund.

Incremental working capital is20% of IP revenue change and30% of silicon revenue change, plus increases in the5%-of-sales operating cash reserve. Net capital investment includes both tangible and intangible productive assets; it is distinct from GAAP gross capex. Initial net-capex intensities6.5%/7.5%/9% decline as implementation matures. The final three years blend into the total reinvestment needed to support terminal growth at12%/18%/24% incremental ROIC. Final reinvestment equals NOPAT×g/ROIC, so growth is not free. Version2 additionally requires a positive analyst net productive-investment floor of2.5% of revenue in each forecast year and terminal year, uniformly on IP and silicon by default. It is a model constraint, not a disclosed or empirically demonstrated engineering requirement. Separate segment-floor inputs can be increased, but inconsistent combinations are rejected. A residual below the floor produces invalid/null output; capital is never clipped upward while keeping an incompatible ROIC. Final silicon revenue must equal its prior year times1+g even when the prior year is zero: both-zero is allowed, zero-to-positive is rejected. This imposes a model transition, not an observed company ROIC. Research costs remain expensed; an R&D-capitalization model would require corresponding asset/amortization and ROIC changes.

WACC11.5%/10%/9% is a scenario choice reflecting business, country, control and execution risk. These are not fitted current betas or a fabricated market-derived cost of capital. Terminal growth must be below WACC and ROIC; all inputs must be finite and within explicit domains. EPS or a market stock quote is never used to calibrate the valuation.

The dynamic treasury starts after known bridge settlements/reserve, retains cash, pays funding interest and tests a5% sales cash floor each year. Incremental operating cash reduces FCFF but remains treasury cash for liquidity testing. Deficits borrow up to1.5×positive EBIT capacity, then issue equity at an explicitly hypothetical$50/ADS with3% fees. This is a scenario financing rule, not a lender commitment or observed issue price. Baseline cases need no external funding. A deliberately stressed case triggers equity; funded cases suppress the headline per-ADS output. Its diluted-denominator diagnostic is not a financing-adjusted fair value because future leverage valuation effects are not comprehensively priced. The treasury uses economic cash-replacement compensation and therefore must not be presented as a GAAP actual cash forecast; real withholding, settlement and SBC timing require a separate cash-ledger forecast.

No discretionary repurchases, dividends or speculative acquisitions are assumed. Version2 preserves all baseline outputs exactly. Its five2%-growth sensitivity cells and two SBC-cost shocks are now invalid rather than priced because the investment floor is violated. Forecasts, valid/invalid sensitivity paths and119 version2 automated checks are stored separately. An independent reviewer checks source evidence, arithmetic and caveats before staging acceptance; this is research quality control, not external audit assurance.

## What changes the case / publication gates

- Verify AGI deliveries becoming recognized, collected revenue; determine gross margin, capacity paid for, yields, customer concentration and cancellation terms.
- Track unrelated licensing/royalty growth, SoftBank contract-asset billing and Arm China collections independently.
- Reconcile SBC expense, taxes and grant/dilution economics after the June award increase. Higher growth does not make awards free.
- Check Q2 FY2027 results when released; as of this cutoff the results page lists November4. Do not fabricate the September quarter.
- Refresh current cash, EDA/lease obligations, completed transactions, exact point-in-time shares and valuation stub before any October price comparison.
- Validate a full ten-year accounting bridge before presenting the older SoftBank revenue series as comparable.
- Do not publish a probability-weighted target without justified probabilities; none are assigned here.
